title: Finite cohomological dimension of finite-type morphisms
statement:
Let $K$ be a field and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism between
schemes of finite type over $K$.

1. **(1)** $\kuncd(f)<\infty$.
1. **(2)** If $K$ is separably
closed, then $\kuncd(X)<\infty$ for every scheme $X$ of finite type
over $K$.

Clause (1) and clause (2) are the classical finiteness of the
cohomological dimension of a scheme of finite type over a field, which
this manuscript already imports elsewhere: the finiteness chain of
the constructibility chapter uses it in [sbc-thm-finiteness-finite-type], and
the Jacobian chapter proves the curve case in
lem:sc-cohomological-dimension, so that the curve and proper
instances are internal to the blueprint. The affine bound
$\kuncd(X)\le\kuncd(K)+\kundim X$ for affine $X$ of finite type over
$K$, which is Tag [0F0V](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0V)
of the Stacks Project, is not needed in this chapter.
(*Source:* Stacks Project, Lemma 59.96.2,
[Tag `0F10`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F10), in
Section 59.96 (finite cohomological dimension): clause (1) is assertion
(1) of that lemma, and clause (2) is
its assertion (2) — which assumes $\kuncd(K)<\infty$ — combined with
[lem-kun-cd-sep-closed-point], where the cohomological dimension of a
separably closed point is computed to be $0$.) In the Stacks Project the proof uses the induction principle of
Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.4.1,
[Tag `08DR`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08DR),
with the affine cases Lemma 59.95.8,
[Tag `0F0X`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0X), for
clause (1) and Proposition 59.95.6,
[Tag `0F0V`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0V), for
clause (2), together with the Mayer–Vietoris sequences Lemma 59.50.2,
[Tag `0EYK`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EYK), and
Lemma 59.50.1, [Tag
`0A50`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A50).

proof.text: First record the geometric hypotheses for the two inductions. A finite-type $K$-scheme has a finite affine cover by spectra of finitely generated $K$-algebras. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $K$), so these rings are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], and their spectra are Noetherian spaces by [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space]. Every open in a Noetherian space is quasi-compact: otherwise the finite unions in an open cover have no maximal member, contradicting the ascending-chain condition on opens. Consequently intersections of two members of this affine cover are quasi-compact; [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion] gives quasi-separatedness. Every open subscheme is quasi-compact, since its intersections with the finitely many Noetherian affine charts are quasi-compact. A quasi-compact open immersion is finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]; composing finite-type maps is checked on affine presentations by taking the union of the two finite sets of algebra generators. Thus every open subscheme is again finite type over $K$. For any morphism between these schemes, the preimage of an affine open is an open in the Noetherian source and hence quasi-compact; for affine opens $U,U'\subseteq X$ mapping into a common affine open of $Y$, the inverse image under its diagonal of $U\times_YU'$ is $U\cap U'$, an open of the Noetherian source and hence quasi-compact. These affine fibre products cover $X\times_YX$, so the diagonal is quasi-compact and the morphism is quasi-separated. These observations apply to $f^{-1}(V)$ for every affine open $V\subseteq Y$ and to all opens used below.

source.place: Tag 0F10, lemma-finite-cd, hypotheses for the induction principle 08DR

proof.text: We make the relative Mayer–Vietoris input explicit without adding a second node for a formal consequence of existing statements. For $h:T\to S$ and $T=A\cup B$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-mayer-vietoris] on $T\times_S W$ for every etale $W\to S$. The localized-site equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open] and [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-over-object-localization] identify its terms with object cohomology of $T\times_S W$, $A\times_S W$, $B\times_S W$ and $(A\cap B)\times_S W$ in their respective small etale sites. The pullback compatibility [lem-weil-pbc-etale-mayer-vietoris-pullback] makes these exact sequences a sequence of presheaves on $S_{\Et}$. Sheafify: exactness is preserved by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact], and [lem-weil-pbc-higher-direct-image-sheafified-presheaf] identifies each sheafified term with the corresponding higher direct image. In particular we obtain the exact segment $$R^{q-1}(h|_{A\cap B})_*(F|_{A\cap B})\longrightarrow R^qh_*F\longrightarrow R^q(h|_A)_*(F|_A)\oplus R^q(h|_B)_*(F|_B),\qquad q\geq1.$$ This is precisely the relative Mayer–Vietoris segment of Tag 0EYK.

source.place: Tag 0EYK, lemma-relative-mayer-vietoris, reconstructed from 0A50 and the sheafified-presheaf description

proof.text: Fix an affine open $V\subseteq Y$ and put $Z=f^{-1}(V)$. For every affine open $W\subseteq Z$, the morphism $g:W\to V$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], since both $W$ and $V$ are affine. Both schemes are finite type over $K$. If $W$ is nonempty, choose an integer $d\geq\dim W$, finite by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. The dimension formula [lem-kun-dimension-formula] gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(w)\leq\dim_wW\leq\dim W\leq d$, since local-ring dimension is nonnegative. Thus $E_d(W)=W$. For any torsion $F$, [lem-kun-affine-direct-image-support-bound] gives $\operatorname{Supp}(R^qg_*F)\subseteq E_{d-q}(V)=\varnothing$ for $q>d$. An empty support means every geometric stalk is zero directly by the existential definition [def-kun-support]. By [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], applied to the map from this sheaf to zero, it is zero. Hence $\kuncd(g)\leq d$. For empty $W$, the only abelian sheaf is zero and the same conclusion holds with bound $0$.

source.place: Tag 0F10, lemma-finite-cd, proof (1), affine case using Tag 0F0X

proof.text: On the qcqs scheme $Z$, let $P(W)$ for a quasi-compact open $W$ mean that $W\to V$ has some finite torsion cohomological-dimension bound, independent of the torsion sheaf. Step 3 proves the affine case. Suppose $P(A)$, $P(B)$ and $P(A\cap B)$ hold, with bounds $a,b,c$, where $A$ is quasi-compact and $B$ is affine. Set $N=\max(a,b,c+1)$. If $q>N$, the two right terms of the exact segment of step 2 vanish because $q>a,b$, and the left term vanishes because $q-1>c$. Hence the middle term vanishes for every torsion sheaf on $A\cup B$; restrictions are torsion by the local-section criterion (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations]: an etale object of an open is an etale object of the whole scheme, and the etale covering and positive annihilating integers supplied for a section remain over that open. This proves $P(A\cup B)$. The induction principle [lem-sc-invert-s-cohomology-induction] now gives $P(Z)$, including the empty case. No intersection of arbitrary affine opens of $Z$ was assumed affine.

source.place: Tag 0F10, lemma-finite-cd, proof (1), induction 08DR and relative Mayer–Vietoris 0EYK

proof.text: Take a finite affine cover $Y=\bigcup_{i=1}^rV_i$ and the bounds $N_i$ supplied by step 4 for $f_i:f^{-1}(V_i)\to V_i$. Let $N=\max(0,N_1,\ldots,N_r)$. The restricted sheaf $F|_{f^{-1}(V_i)}$ is torsion by the restriction argument of step 4. For a geometric point $\bar y$ in $V_i$, the pointed etale neighbourhoods factoring through $V_i$ are cofinal among all pointed etale neighbourhoods in $Y$: replace any neighbourhood $W$ by the open $W\times_YV_i$, which still contains its marked point. The colimit in [lem-kun-cd-stalk-criterion] is therefore the same for $f$ and $f_i$ at this point. For $q>N$ it vanishes for $f_i$ and hence for $f$. Applying that criterion at every geometric point yields $R^qf_*F=0$ for every torsion $F$, proving clause (1). If $Y$ is empty, so is $X$, and use $N=0$.

source.place: Tag 0F10, lemma-finite-cd, proof (1), "We may assume Y is affine"; made uniform over a finite cover

proof.text: For clause (2), [lem-kun-cd-sep-closed-point] gives $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(K)\leq0$. For a nonempty affine finite-type $K$-scheme $W$, [thm-sc-affine-torsion-cd] with $c=0$ gives $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(W)\leq\dim W$, which is finite by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]; the torsion vanishing conventions of [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd] and [def-kun-cd] quantify over the same torsion abelian etale sheaves. The empty affine scheme has bound $0$. On $X$ use the property $Q(W)$ that all torsion sheaf cohomology on $W$ vanishes above some integer bound. If $Q(A),Q(B),Q(A\cap B)$ hold with bounds $a,b,c$, then for $q>\max(a,b,c+1)$ the exact Mayer–Vietoris segment has zero end groups $H^{q-1}(A\cap B,F|)$ and $H^q(A,F|)\oplus H^q(B,F|)$, so $H^q(A\cup B,F)=0$. All restricted sheaves remain torsion by the local-section argument of step 4 using [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations]. Applying [lem-sc-invert-s-cohomology-induction] on the qcqs finite-type scheme $X$ proves $Q(X)$, and therefore clause (2).
